title: Choose the visual world for JARVIS
question: The roll assigned Night Concourse. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. All of them stay simple, dark and futuristic.

options.label: Night Concourse
options.lineage: Airport wayfinding signs (Kinneir & Calvert, Schiphol) on backlit night panels
options.thesis: Every screen is a sign: one plain sentence saying where your PC stands and which way to go next.
options.viewport: Home is one large sign: status sentence in big type, then arrow rows (Set up voice, Run a scan, Ask JARVIS), each with a pictogram, like a concourse sign.
options.risk: Reads as transit cosplay if the arrows and pictograms stop doing real wayfinding work.

raised.raise: When JARVIS wakes, the listening state takes over the whole window: one thing at a time, nothing else competing.
Neutrals are locked to one stepped panel ramp; the only other colours are the route colours that carry meaning.
Every sign panel snaps to one module grid with hairline seams, so the whole app reads as one signage system.

options.label: Glass Cockpit
options.lineage: Airbus ECAM and modern glass-cockpit avionics
options.thesis: Your PC as an aircraft's systems page: instruments, caution levels and step-by-step checklists.
options.viewport: Home is a systems page: CPU, memory, disk and network as instruments, with a caution list below that turns into a checklist when you act.
options.risk: Also the direction most 'futuristic dashboard' runs land on: dark screen with glowing green and amber.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: Jet-age airline ticket wallets and coupons
options.thesis: Every fix is a coupon: approved, used or void gets stamped on it, and nothing ever disappears.
options.viewport: Activity & safety shows each action as a coupon, stamped APPROVED, USED or VOID, filed in order.
options.case: Fuses well for approvals and the audit trail; loses on 'simple and futuristic' because it reads as paper and print.
options.risk: Feels retro and papery instead of futuristic.

options.label: Full-screen Feed
options.thesis: One item fills the screen; flick to the next.
options.viewport: One finding per screen with an action rail on the right.
options.case: A PC health app needs overview and comparison, which one-at-a-time hides.
options.kept: The wake/listening moment owns the whole window.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Translucent sheets over an eleven-step tonal ramp; hatching shows load.
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets for each subsystem with hatched load regions.
options.case: Too specialist to be easy to understand.
options.kept: One strict tonal ramp as the only neutrals.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: Near-white stock, registration marks and hairline credits.
options.viewport: Findings as printed plates with credits rows.
options.case: Light, editorial and print-like; not futuristic.
options.kept: One module grid built from hairlines.
options.risk: Reads as a magazine, not a PC tool.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.thesis: Each subsystem is a coloured land lobe on a cream sea.
options.viewport: A map of your PC with CPU, memory and disk as islands.
options.case: Playful and warm; fights both 'futuristic' and the evidence-first tone.
options.kept: One shape can drive layout and state together.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: One plant through its seasons at a fixed scale.
options.viewport: Your PC's history as seasonal plates.
options.case: Cream and botanical; nothing about it reads futuristic or technical.
options.kept: Fixed-scale comparison across time (useful later for history views).

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Windows 11 style dashboard: sidebar, cards and a blue accent, done well.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar on the left, a grid of health cards on Home, charts on Monitor.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every system utility and gaming-laptop app.
